ConfigCheckOut.description:
What a launch of this config would meet, without spending one.

`ok` is false when a launch, benchmark or contender with this config would
be refused (`problems`). `warnings` never refuse anything: flags the
platform's catalog does not know (the engine may still accept them) and
how the config steps outside the declared space (`deviations`).
ConfigCheckOut.title: ConfigCheckOut

ContendersEcho.description:
The PUT response: what was accepted, and what was refused and why —
rejected entries are echoed rather than 422ing the whole list, so one bad
spec cannot cost a policy its good ones.
ContendersEcho.title: ContendersEcho

DigestIn.description:
What a night learned, in the policy's words: written once its search is
over, for other campaigns to read through GET /history. The conditions it
was learned under are the platform's to state, not the policy's.
DigestIn.title: DigestIn

DimCoverage.description:
What a policy has explored along one declared axis.

Keyed by the platform's own parameter name (`space.swept_keys()`), so the
two sides speak one coordinate system. Discrete points go in `tried_values`;
a continuous/model-based sweep reports the interval(s) it has covered in
`tried_ranges` ([{"min": .., "max": ..}]). `skipped_values` is intent — a
region the policy deliberately will not try (e.g. tp=1 OOMs) — so coverage
shows it as "skipped", not "unexplored".
DimCoverage.title: DimCoverage

HistoryConditions.description: Under what a night's findings hold, from the platform's own records.
HistoryConditions.title: HistoryConditions

HistoryVerdict.description: One config the platform validated at the end of the night.
HistoryVerdict.title: HistoryVerdict

ManifestProduction.description:
Production: what serves today, as the platform launches it when it
measures production next to the contenders.
ManifestProduction.title: ManifestProduction

PolicyCoverage.description:
The policy's own account of how far it has searched — the *supplement*
the platform cannot derive from the trial ledger: a completion estimate for
an infinite/model-based space, deliberate skips, and self-served work the
platform never saw as a trial. Advisory: the platform trusts its own
ledger for what was actually measured and badges this as self-reported.
PolicyCoverage.title: PolicyCoverage

VocabularyOut.description:
The flags and environment variables the campaign's engine image reads
(1.5), best recommendation first.

`status` is "ok", "partial" (some of it could not be read; `notes` says
what), or "none" (nothing has been dumped from this image yet). Each entry:
{kind: flag|env, name, type, default, choices, help, help_source, where,
level: high|mid|low|unknown, when}. `level` is the platform's hand-written
recommendation, `when` the situation it helps in; an entry labeled only for
other hardware is left out.
VocabularyOut.title: VocabularyOut

info.description:
Automated parameter search for LLM inference engines (sglang, vLLM).

A **campaign** searches a **search space** against an **objective**, on machines
the platform has been **leased**. Each point becomes a **run**: a container is
launched with those engine arguments, benchmarked by LLMBench, and scored.

### Authentication

Two credentials, both accepted on the lease endpoints:

* **`Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`** — for people. `POST /api/auth/login`.
* **`X-API-Key: atk_…`** — for services. Minted at `POST /api/api-keys`, shown
  once. Everything else takes the bearer token only.

### Integrating a fleet manager

The **machine leases** section is the surface built for external callers. The
short version:

```
POST /api/machines/lease           {"name": "node-24", "host": "…", "due_at": …}
GET  /api/machines/node-24/lease     -> readiness: busy | idle | returnable
POST /api/machines/node-24/lease/end {"mode": "polite"}
```

Ending a lease is asynchronous. The machine is yours when `readiness` reads
`returnable` — by which point the production service we found on it has been
put back and verified.
info.title: LLM AutoTune

get.description:
The benchmark in full: every scenario, every concurrency level, latency
percentiles, the best level that met the gate. `status` says whether it is
measured yet.
The benchmark platform's own result payload, exactly as harvested.

post.description:
Everything a launch of this config would meet — refusals, the canonical
echo, the rendered command, catalog warnings, deviations — without
spending a launch. Never 422s: the answer is the point.

get.description:
What the campaign's engine image reads, filtered: `kind`, a substring
of the name or help (`query`), and the lowest `level` wanted ("mid" =
high and mid).

Other campaigns' nights, newest first: what each policy wrote it
learned, under which conditions, and what the platform validated. Only
campaigns of the same owner; this campaign's own nights are in /state.
Findings from another workload or image are hints, not facts here.

get.description:
What the launch actually ran on: engine, torch and CUDA versions, image
digest, card. Recorded once the engine is up; fill a contender's
`launch_spec.environment` from it to make its verdict promotable.

The engine's log: live from its container while it runs, the saved copy
after. Startup errors, OOM traces and the engine's own throughput lines
are here — the evidence a failed or slow launch leaves.

of this session; accepted until the session ends.
